title: Ivo and the Debt
premise: Marguerite Halloran, a private security contractor who guards clients nobody trusts, is hired to protect a tech executive whose voiceprint unlocks a black server in Lisbon — a server holding proof that a summit's security apparatus has been sold. When the defector who built the server surfaces, Marguerite realizes she's not being paid to protect anyone; she's the extraction team, and the defector may be bait meant to flush out everyone who knows. Torn between her contract, the lover she's lied to for years, and a debt she owes from a job gone wrong, Marguerite chooses justice outside the law: she burns the server publicly at the summit's opening, exposes the buyers, and walks away from the industry — alive, disowned, and finally honest.
about_author: Ansel Joubert is the pen name of a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade documenting how private security firms operate in the gaps between jurisdictions. They write from a coastal town where the fog arrives earlier every year.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet her mid-rotation guarding a paranoid fintech CEO in Geneva, her go-bag packed under the hotel bed, rehearsing the lie she'll tell her partner Ivo about another missed anniversary. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — she's excellent at a job that requires her to trust no one.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her client's biometric vault pings an authentication request from Lisbon using his stolen voiceprint. He panics; she traces it to a dead man's server farm. First hint that her firm, Corvid Risk, already knew. Emotional beat: the cold drop when competence meets betrayal.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Dual POV opens on Ivo, a human-rights lawyer in The Hague, receiving an anonymous file about the same server. Back in Geneva, Marguerite's handler rewrites her contract: escort duty becomes 'asset recovery.' Emotional beat: two people who love each other being aimed at the same secret from opposite ends.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The anonymous contact reveals herself: Dr. Lena Vasquez, architect of the server, willing to testify before the summit convenes in nine days — if someone extracts her from Tangier. Ivo recognizes Corvid's fingerprints on her redactions. Emotional beat: hope arriving wrapped in a warning.

chapters.title: Debt
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, flashback braided into present. We learn what she owes: three years ago in Kinshasa, a Corvid op killed civilians, and Lena Vasquez was the analyst whose report she buried to save her own contract. Emotional beat: guilt as muscle memory — the lie polished until it gleams.

chapters.title: Tangier, Low Tide
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She arrives in Tangier for 'recovery' and finds surveillance teams from three different employers watching the same safehouse. She makes contact with Lena through a fish-market cutout and realizes the defector expected her by name. Emotional beat: hunter discovering she's also prey.

chapters.title: What the Server Holds
chapters.summary: Lena's POV (first appearance). Inside the safehouse, Lena shows Marguerite fragments: summit security contracts auctioned to a syndicate, kill-lists priced per delegate. She names the price of her testimony — Marguerite's buried Kinshasa report, made public. Emotional beat: the debt called in, face to face.

chapters.title: Two Phones
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ivo calls Marguerite about his anonymous source; both realize they're working the same case and neither says so. Each lies fluently, lovingly. Emotional beat: love against duty dramatized as parallel phone calls with mirrored omissions.

chapters.title: Corvid Calls
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her handler, Devereux, flies in personally — unprecedented — and offers her a clean slate if she delivers Lena alone. He mentions Ivo's name casually, a threat wearing a courtesy. Emotional beat: the employer showing its teeth behind a smile.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Lena and Marguerite's POV. They test whether Lena's location was leaked deliberately; the safehouse's landlord turns out to be a retired syndicate courier. Conclusion: yes, Lena is bait — but for whom? Possibly for Ivo's tribunal contacts. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: Extraction, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Action centerpiece, Marguerite's POV. Night move to the port goes wrong: a rival team hits the safehouse early. Marguerite gets Lena out through the medina but takes a graze wound; a Corvid asset lets them go — someone inside is hedging. Emotional beat: survival bought with a favor she can't name yet.

chapters.title: Confession at Sea
chapters.summary: Two-hander on a chartered boat, alternating POV. Marguerite tells Lena the full truth of Kinshasa; Lena admits she chose Marguerite deliberately — redemption or ruin, either would serve. Meanwhile Ivo lands in Algeciras chasing their trail. Emotional beat: truth as the only currency left.

chapters.title: The Hague Interlude
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reaches his old mentor at the tribunal, learns the summit's host state will block any testimony that implicates its own contractors. He must choose between procedure and leak. Emotional beat: a lawful man watching law fail in real time.

chapters.title: Reunion, Loaded
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ivo finds them in Cádiz; the reunion is tender and armed — he's brought questions, she's brought a gun she doesn't hide anymore. He offers the legal route; Devereux's deadline offers none. Emotional beat: love refusing to look away from what the beloved has done.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She identifies the Corvid asset who spared them: Reyes, her oldest colleague, feeding Devereux just enough to stay alive. Reyes warns her the syndicate has bought a delegate — the summit itself is the target, and Lena's death would bury the evidence. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as its own kind of debt.

chapters.title: Nine Hours
chapters.summary: Ticking-clock chapter, rapid POV rotation. Plan crystallizes: get Lena into the summit perimeter, not out of the country; broadcast the server live during the opening plenary. Ivo works credentials; Reyes covers their exit; Marguerite plans for the possibility she doesn't come back. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Perimeter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Infiltration of the summit venue via a service corridor she helped design years ago — the industry's own habits turned against it. Devereux's team is already inside; he anticipated her. Emotional beat: the past as ambush.

chapters.title: The Debt Paid
chapters.summary: Climax part one, Marguerite and Lena's POV. Confrontation with Devereux in the comms room; Marguerite offers him the choice he never gave Kinshasa's civilians. He refuses; Reyes' distraction buys seconds. Lena begins the upload as alarms cascade. Emotional beat: choosing justice over survival, consciously.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax part two, ensemble POV. The server's contents hit every screen in the plenary hall mid-speech; delegates scatter, the syndicate's buyers are named, and Ivo's mentor's office receives the certified copy simultaneously. Devereux is arrested by the host state's own panicked security. Emotional beat: catharsis — the truth landing like weather.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unpacked
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Hearings begin; Lena testifies; Marguerite declines immunity in exchange for silence about Corvid's other clients — she won't trade one silence for another. Reyes disappears with a pension and no forwarding address. Emotional beat: justice partial, real, unsatisfying, necessary.

chapters.title: The Empty Bag
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She unpacks the go-bag for the first time in eleven years, item by item, each object a year of readiness for flight. Ivo watches without helping. Emotional beat: belonging chosen rather than earned — staying as an act of courage.

chapters.title: Ivo and the Debt
chapters.summary: Final chapter, shared POV closing on Ivo. Months later, a new client approaches Marguerite with an offer she declines by name, out loud, in daylight. The last scene: the two of them at a kitchen table, the debt acknowledged, the lie retired. Emotional beat: quiet ending — love that survived the truth.
